content: I am different from other people: I drink from the Great Mother's breast.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

In Lao Tzu's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: How can you create a moment of stillness today to reconnect with your deeper sense of purpose?
